children: South Korean consumer electronics major LG Electronics, the promoter of LG Electronics India Ltd, is looking to sell up to 2% of the company's total equity through a block deal worth up to ₹2,320.5 crore, according to the deal details.

The floor price for the offer has been set at ₹1,709.30 per share, representing a discount of around 6% to the stock's last closing price. The offer involves the sale of up to 13.58 million shares. The seller will be subject to a 180-day lock-up period on any further sale of shares.
This follows LG Electronics' plan to sell up to a 2% stake in the company through open-market transactions to meet minimum public shareholding (MPS) requirements.
The company said the promoter intends to divest up to 13,575,447 equity shares, representing up to 2% of the company’s total issued and paid-up equity share capital.

LG Electronics Inc. currently holds 85% of the total issued and paid-up equity share capital of LG Electronics India. Following the completion of the proposed divestment, its holding would come down to 83%, according to the filing.

The proposed transaction is being undertaken to meet the minimum public shareholding requirement applicable to the listed entity. The company said the promoter has conveyed its intention to sell the shares held by it for this purpose.

Earlier this month, the company reported its September quarter performance, with revenue and EBITDA coming in ahead of CNBC-TV18 poll estimates, while net profit was broadly in line with expectations.

Revenue rose 19.5% year-on-year to ₹7,380 crore, while EBITDA increased 27.9% to ₹701 crore. EBITDA margin expanded to 9.5% from 8.9% a year ago, while net profit grew 27.5% to ₹489 crore. The company’s board also approved a foray into a new line of business, adding a new area of operations as it looks to expand its business portfolio.
Shares of LG Electronics India Ltd ended at ₹1,819.70, up by ₹41.65, or 2.34%, on the BSE.

title: LG Electronics Block Deal: Promoter likely to sell 2% stake at ₹1,709 floor price to meet MPS norms
